title: Join two boards on three glued dowels, pressing them together evenly
instruction: Join the pale board to the dark board on the three dowels so their ends meet flat on the bench, then let go.
context: Carpenters (SOC 47-2031, about 900,000 US workers, BLS) and cabinetmakers join boards end to end on glued dowels in face frames, rails and furniture as a regular duty. The two loose boards are held one in each hand and brought together so three dowels enter three sockets at once. Pressed with one end first, the boards twist and the dowels bind in their sockets, leaving the joint wedged half open. Both hands are needed: each board lies beside its own arm, 0.51 m from the other board's seam end, and the arm cannot carry its board to the far board and press it on.
setup: Station table, positions in metres, x forward from the arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up; the table top is at z 0.7475. The bench is a waxed laminate top, friction about 0.25 against wood. (1) Pale board: birch, 18 x 80 x 150 mm, 123 g, colour sRGB (0.87, 0.74, 0.52), centre (0.36, -0.33), long axis along y. Three beech dowels, 8 mm diameter, 20 mm long with a 0.6 mm stepped tip, tan (0.72, 0.50, 0.25), are glued into its +y end at x -25, 0 and +25 mm from its centre line, 9 mm above the bench. (2) Dark board: walnut, 18 x 80 x 150 mm, 140 g, colour (0.36, 0.24, 0.16), centre (0.36, +0.33), long axis along y. Its -y end has three round dowel sockets, 22 mm deep, at the same pitch and height; in the simulation each is a ring of 16 thin boxes around an 8.4 mm bore (0.2 mm clearance a side). (3) Real build: 8.0 mm beech dowels pushed 20 mm (dry hand-pressed) into 8.0 mm drilled holes; sockets drilled with an 8.0 mm brad-point bit 22 mm deep, the hole measuring 8.0 to 8.1 mm (a snug slip fit, 0 to 0.1 mm clearance across), checked with 8.1 mm go and 8.3 mm no-go pin gauges; bench friction checked with a spring scale (about 0.3 N to slide the 123 g board). (4) Nothing clamps, jigs or stops either board. Seat line: y 0; the left arm base is at y +0.305, the right at y -0.305. Ready pose for both arms.
scoring: Only the final state counts; nothing reached earlier earns credit, and no damage condition is scored (nothing can break). Every control step the scorer measures the two seam-end corner gaps (negative when the boards overlap), the height difference of the boards, the sideways offset, the yaw and each board's tilt from the two board poses; the rung is read from the last measurement. Every rung below 1.0 needs both corner gaps at least -2 mm, the boards within 2 mm of the same height (a stacked board fails) and both flat within 3 deg. 0.25: at the end both corner gaps at most 19 mm (tips in), offset at most 1 mm, yaw at most 2 deg. 0.5: both corner gaps at most 10 mm, offset and yaw as above. 0.75: seated: both corner gaps at most 0.5 mm, edges flush within 1 mm. 1.0: also both grippers at least 30 mm from both boards and moving under 10 mm/s for the final 1 s, boards still under 5 mm/s. Real trial: a feeler gauge at the two seam corners, a try square or straightedge on the long edge for the 1 mm offset, a straightedge across both top faces with a 2 mm feeler for the height bound, a protractor for 3 deg, a tape for the 30 mm clearance, and a 60 fps overhead video over a 1 mm grid for the final state and stillness.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Pull the boards apart and wipe the round sockets and dowels clean (dry fit, no glue). Set the pale board with its dowel end toward the middle and the dark board with its socket end toward the middle, centres at (0.36, -0.33) and (0.36, +0.33), edges square to the x axis on taped outlines, 0.51 m between the seam ends.
fidelity: Real boards and dowels at true size and mass. Real sockets are round 8.0 mm drilled holes (about 8.1 mm, snug slip fit); the simulated socket is a round bore 8.4 mm across built from 16 boxes, 0.15 to 0.2 mm a side looser than real because of contact offsets and 0.1 mm vision alignment, and press-fit friction and glue are not modelled; the wedge is geometric. Boards are rigid at one friction (0.25) on the bench, and the grip is a 1.5 mm squeeze of the 80 mm width.
scores: Not re-run on this revision (no simulator time left); previous revision: demo 1.0
